- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model overcorrects in next 3–7 days; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 3–5 days.
- If model forecast is consistently above true for 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If model forecast is consistently below true for 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: add 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses 1–2 week mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 14-day moving average of true values.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low (e.g., 0.8, 0.2, 0.8, 0.2), model tends to lag; add 1–3% to forecast for next 2–4 days to catch momentum.
